narrative_content: The jagged obsidian shoreline drops sharply into a swirling, metallic expanse of the ferrofluid sea, its surface rippling with impossible geometric waves. Static electricity crackles in the dense air, illuminating the cavern with erratic, blue-white strobes. A thick, coppery mist clings to the rocky outcroppings, tasting faintly of ozone. Ryn grimaces as the air temperature spikes, sweat beading on their brow. The Magnetohydrodynamic Kelvin-Helmholtz shear is tearing at the boundary layer, a chaotic vortex of magnetic force. They reach out, gripping the obsidian outcropping to steady themselves against the sudden pull. 'Silas!' Ryn shouts over the rhythmic sloshing. 'I need a vector on that surge before it swallows the probe!' With a final, desperate wrench of the containment lever, Ryn locks the field in place. They turn, chest heaving, and toss the calibration baton through the crackling air to Silas. 'It's holding, but barely. Your turn, archivist. What do those sensors say?'
